systematic_read.airway_lungs: CURRENT: Trachea is roughly midline allowing for rotation. Lung volumes are low. Diffuse bilateral hazy and reticular opacity, most marked in the perihilar and mid zones, with denser opacity at both bases. No pleural line is seen, but the film is supine. PRIOR: Trachea is roughly midline. Lungs are better inflated and largely clear, with mildly prominent perihilar and right lower zone markings. No focal consolidation, discrete nodule or pneumothorax is seen.
systematic_read.mediastinum_hila: CURRENT: Upper mediastinum looks wide on an AP supine film. Both hila are indistinct, with surrounding hazy opacity. PRIOR: Mediastinal contour is within expected limits for the projection. Hila are mildly prominent and look vascular, with no clear one-sided enlargement.
systematic_read.pleura: CURRENT: Both costophrenic angles are hazy and both hemidiaphragms are partly obscured; layering pleural fluid is possible on a supine film. No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax, with limited sensitivity when supine. PRIOR: Right costophrenic angle appears clear. Left costophrenic angle is seen low on the film and is not sharply defined. No pneumothorax.
systematic_read.heart: CURRENT: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged, on an AP supine film where it is magnified. Heart borders are partly blurred by adjacent lung opacity. PRIOR: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged on a PA film, with a prominent left heart border.
systematic_read.diaphragm_below: CURRENT: Both hemidiaphragms are elevated with low volumes and partly obscured. Free gas under the diaphragm cannot be assessed on a supine film. PRIOR: Right hemidiaphragm is well defined. Left hemidiaphragm is partly obscured behind the heart. No free gas is seen.
systematic_read.bones_soft_tissue: CURRENT: No displaced rib fracture or destructive bone lesion is seen at this resolution. No soft tissue gas. PRIOR: Degenerative change in the spine and shoulders. No displaced rib fracture or destructive bone lesion is seen. No soft tissue gas.
systematic_read.devices: CURRENT: Left chest wall cardiac device generator with transvenous leads. One lead has a coil over the right side of the mediastinum (expected region of the SVC), one coiled lead projects over the lower heart, and small electrode markers project over the left heart. Lead configuration is broadly similar to the prior allowing for projection. A vertical linear density projects over the tracheal air column and could be an endotracheal tube. A further linear density over the right upper mediastinum and a looped density over the upper abdomen could be a central line or enteric tube, or external. These are not confirmed at this resolution. External monitoring leads are present. PRIOR: Left chest wall cardiac device generator with the same lead configuration. No tubes or central lines.

findings.description: Diffuse hazy and reticular opacity in the right perihilar and mid zone with indistinct vessels. Part of a bilateral pattern, which may reflect interstitial or alveolar fluid; other diffuse processes are not excluded.
findings.evidence: The right mid zone on the prior shows only mildly prominent markings with clear lung between them. The current shows confluent haze that blurs the vessels and the hilum. The opacity extends above the basal zones, where low volumes alone would not be expected to produce it. Supine position and lower volumes contribute to some of the difference.

findings.description: Hazy and reticular opacity in the left perihilar and mid zone with indistinct vessels, part of the same bilateral pattern.
findings.evidence: The left mid zone on the prior is largely clear. The current shows perihilar haze and coarse markings extending to the lateral lung. Supine position and lower volumes contribute to some of the difference.

findings.description: Hazy opacity at the right base, partly obscuring the right hemidiaphragm.
findings.evidence: The right base and hemidiaphragm are well defined on the prior. On the current the right base is dense and the hemidiaphragm is partly lost. The current film is supine with low volumes, which crowds the base and may mimic or exaggerate basal opacity.

findings.description: Retrocardiac and left basal opacity, obscuring the left hemidiaphragm.
findings.evidence: The left base behind the heart is denser on the current, and the hemidiaphragm is not seen. The heart shadow is magnified on AP and volumes are low, which may account for part of this. The retrocardiac region was also partly obscured on the prior.

findings.description: Hazy right costophrenic angle with graded basal density. A layering pleural effusion is possible.
findings.evidence: The right costophrenic angle appears clear on the upright prior. On the supine current the angle is hazy. Fluid layers posteriorly when supine, so its presence and amount cannot be judged against an upright film.

findings.description: Hazy left costophrenic angle. A layering pleural effusion is possible.
findings.evidence: The left costophrenic angle is not sharply defined on either study. Upright versus supine position prevents comparison of the amount of fluid.

findings.description: Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both studies.
findings.evidence: The heart is enlarged on the PA prior. It looks larger on the current, but the current is AP supine with low volumes, which magnifies the heart shadow. Size change is not reported across different projections.

findings.description: Left chest wall cardiac device with transvenous leads: a coil over the right mediastinum, a coiled lead over the lower heart, and electrode markers over the left heart.
findings.evidence: The generator and the same lead configuration are present on both studies. Apparent shifts in lead position are in keeping with the change in projection, position and inspiration. No visible lead discontinuity at this resolution.

findings.description: Linear densities over the tracheal air column, the right upper mediastinum and the upper abdomen. These could be an endotracheal tube and an enteric tube or central line, or external tubing.
findings.evidence: These densities are not present on the prior. On the current they overlap the device leads, external wires and the spine, so their presence and tip positions cannot be confirmed on this image.

cant_determine.question: Has the heart size changed?
cant_determine.reason: Prior is PA and current is AP supine with low volumes. AP projection and low inspiration magnify the heart shadow.
cant_determine.recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able. Echocardiography if clinically relevant.

cant_determine.question: Is the upper mediastinum widened?
cant_determine.reason: The current film is AP supine with mild rotation, which widens the mediastinal shadow. Device leads cross the region.
cant_determine.recommend: Repeat upright PA film when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.

cant_determine.question: Are pleural effusions present, and have they changed?
cant_determine.reason: The current film is supine, so fluid layers posteriorly and shows only as haze. The prior is upright. The amounts are not comparable.
cant_determine.recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.

cant_determine.question: Do the basal opacities reflect consolidation, collapse, layering fluid or low volumes?
cant_determine.reason: Low inspiration and supine position crowd the lower zones and mimic basal opacity. The magnified heart hides the left base.
cant_determine.recommend: Repeat film with good inspiration when the patient is able, or CT chest.

cant_determine.question: Is there a pneumothorax?
cant_determine.reason: No pleural line is seen, but on a supine film air collects anteriorly and at the bases and may not show. A skin fold or linen line and external wires cross the chest.
cant_determine.recommend: Upright or decubitus film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.

cant_determine.question: Are an endotracheal tube, enteric tube or central line present, and where are the tips?
cant_determine.reason: Linear densities over the trachea, right upper mediastinum and upper abdomen overlap device leads, external wires and the spine. The image is low resolution.
cant_determine.recommend: Review the source image in PACS with edge enhancement and correlate with the bedside record of lines and tubes. Confirm tip positions before use.

cant_determine.question: Are there small lung nodules, or lesions behind the heart or generator?
cant_determine.reason: Diffuse opacity on the current film, the device generator over the left upper chest and the enlarged heart all hide lung. The AP portable film is lower quality than the PA prior.
cant_determine.recommend: CT chest if clinically relevant, or repeat PA and lateral after the diffuse opacity clears.

cant_determine.question: Is there free gas under the diaphragm?
cant_determine.reason: The current film is supine. Free gas does not collect under the diaphragm in this position.
cant_determine.recommend: Upright or decubitus film if there is clinical concern.

a.limits: This is a blind first read with no indication and no dates, drafted for resident and attending review. The prior is PA and the current is AP supine portable with lower lung volumes, so comparison is limited. No size change is reported for the heart, mediastinum or any lesion. Supine position limits assessment for pleural effusion, pneumothorax and free gas. The images are reduced resolution; fine detail, lead integrity and tube or line tip positions should be checked on the source images in PACS. No measurements are given. All findings are descriptive and none is a diagnosis.

systematic_read.pleura: CURRENT: Right costophrenic angle and right hemidiaphragm are obscured by hazy basal opacity. Left costophrenic angle is hazy. systematic_read.diaphragm_below: CURRENT: Both hemidiaphragms are elevated with low volumes. The right hemidiaphragm outline is obscured. Free gas cannot be assessed on a supine film. A tubular density projects over the upper abdomen in the midline, possibly an enteric tube or external tubing. PRIOR: Both domes are defined, right slightly higher than left. No free gas under the diaphragm.
systematic_read.bones_soft_tissue: CURRENT: No displaced rib fracture seen on this limited portable film. No soft tissue gas seen. PRIOR: No displaced rib fracture. No destructive bone lesion seen. Degenerative change at the shoulders. No soft tissue gas.
systematic_read.devices: CURRENT: Left chest wall cardiac device generator with transvenous leads. Coil segments project over the right mediastinal border (superior vena cava region) and over the lower heart (right ventricle region). Additional lead electrodes project over the left heart border, likely a coronary sinus lead. A lead with a curved tip projects over the right atrial region. Probable endotracheal tube over the trachea. Possible enteric tube over the upper abdomen. ECG electrodes are external. PRIOR: Same left chest wall generator and lead configuration: superior vena cava coil, right ventricular coil, and electrodes over the left heart border. No endotracheal or enteric tube.

findings.description: Hazy and coarse reticular perihilar opacity in the right mid zone, extending toward the upper and lower zones. Consistent with interstitial or alveolar fluid. Other diffuse airspace processes are not excluded.

Supine position and low volumes add vascular crowding, but the opacity reaches the mid and upper zones, where low volumes explain less.

findings.description: Hazy left lower zone and retrocardiac opacity with an indistinct left costophrenic angle.
findings.evidence: Prior PA shows a clear left lower zone lateral to the enlarged heart. Current shows hazy density at the left base. Low volumes, supine position and the enlarged heart shadow may account for some or all of it.

findings.description: Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both studies.
findings.evidence: Prior PA shows an enlarged heart. Current is AP supine with low volumes, which magnifies the heart shadow, so interval change in size cannot be judged.

findings.evidence: No tube projects over the trachea on the prior. On the current film a vertical tubular density overlies the midline trachea at the thoracic inlet. The tip position needs confirmation by the radiologist.

findings.evidence: The generator and lead configuration are the same on both studies. The differences in apparent generator size and lead projection are in keeping with AP magnification and supine positioning. No lead discontinuity is seen at this resolution.

cant_determine.recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Repeat the film if the tube positions remain unclear.

cant_determine.reason: A supine film does not show subdiaphragmatic free gas reliably.
cant_determine.recommend: Upright or left lateral decubitus film, or CT, if there is clinical concern.

b.limits: Blind read of two frontal chest radiographs with no indication or dates. Prior is PA. Current is AP supine portable with low lung volumes. Projection, position and inspiration all differ, so comparison is limited and no size change is reported for the heart, the mediastinum or any opacity. The images are downsampled, so fine detail (lead integrity, tube tips, small nodules, subtle fractures) needs review on the source images in PACS. The device generator obscures part of the left lung on both studies. No lateral view. This is a draft for resident and attending review.

indication_pass.question: What on the film could account for the shortness of breath, and is there any visible chest or bone abnormality relevant to the history of prostate cancer?
indication_pass.answer: Hazy and reticular opacity around both hila and in both mid zones has increased from the prior, with bibasal opacity and an enlarged cardiac silhouette. This pattern may reflect interstitial or alveolar fluid, and other diffuse processes are not excluded. No discrete lung mass or definite destructive rib lesion is seen, but the supine portable technique, diffuse opacity and reduced resolution limit this, and pleural effusion and pneumothorax remain undetermined.

added_findings.description: Mottled, heterogeneous density projecting over the right glenoid and scapular neck region on the current film. It could be a projectional effect from arm position and the overlying ECG electrode, or altered bone texture. This does not settle the open question about bone lesions. No definite sclerotic or destructive lesion is identified in the visible ribs, clavicles or spine at this resolution.
added_findings.evidence: On the prior PA the right shoulder girdle shows no similar mottled density, but the arm position and projection differ. On the current AP supine film an oval area of granular density overlies the right scapula just above an ECG electrode. Overlap with the electrode and reduced resolution prevent a confident call. Review on the source images in PACS is needed.
